chunks: And by this chain, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurāra, who said:

I asked Abu Jaʿfar (AS) about some people who say that the ears are part of the face and the back of the ears is part of the head. He replied: "Neither washing nor wiping is required of them [the ears]."

And what he mentioned — that one takes the water to wash the right hand with the right hand, then transfers it to the left hand, and then washes the right hand — is supported by what was contained in the earlier narration concerning the description of the wudu of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), and this further confirms it.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful — honorific title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS)
key_terms.الْأُذُنَيْنِ: the two ears — dual form; the subject of the juristic dispute
key_terms.غَسْلٌ: ritual washing — complete wetting of a limb as required in wudu
key_terms.مَسْحٌ: ritual wiping — passing a moist hand over a surface (as over the head) in wudu

ai.seo_question: Is it obligatory to wash or wipe the ears during wudu according to Imam al-Baqir (AS)?
ai.summary: Zurara narrates asking Imam al-Baqir (AS) about the position of those who claim the ears form part of the face (requiring washing) and the back of the ears form part of the head (requiring wiping) in wudu. The Imam ruled unequivocally that neither washing nor wiping is required for the ears. Al-Tusi then notes that the method of taking water with the right hand, transferring it to the left, and then washing the right hand is further corroborated and reinforced by the earlier narration describing the wudu of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS).
